response.sql:
WITH execution_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    ordersmark,
    COUNT(*) as exec_count
  FROM orderexecutions
  GROUP BY ordersmark
),
total_count AS (
  SELECT SUM(exec_count) as total_exec FROM execution_counts
),
with_share AS (
  SELECT 
    ec.ordersmark,
    ec.exec_count,
    CAST(ec.exec_count AS REAL) / CAST(tc.total_exec AS REAL) as share
  FROM execution_counts ec
  CROSS JOIN total_count tc
),
avg_share AS (
  SELECT AVG(share) as avg_share_val
  FROM with_share
)
SELECT 
  ws.ordersmark,
  ws.exec_count,
  ws.share,
  ws.share - av.avg_share_val as share_minus_avg
FROM with_share ws
CROSS JOIN avg_share av
ORDER BY share_minus_avg DESC, CASE WHEN ws.ordersmark IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: By 'executions lacking a reference', ordersmark is NULL; SQLite naturally groups NULL values together in GROUP BY.
By 'average share across order references', the request means the arithmetic mean of individual shares (not a uniform expectation like 1/N).

alternatives.interpretation: If 'missing values last' requires NULL ordersmarks to be placed at the end of output *after* selecting the top 10 (rather than sorted naturally by share_minus_avg), apply a secondary sort to move any NULL to the absolute end.
